Episode 132: Massacre and Something Strange...(5)
What Midor Elna took out looked like a slightly smaller cube than a fist.
Midor's face was full of anticipation as he looked at the object. The cube had a mysterious blue glow that seemed to wrap around it.
'Finally, I can take revenge for my brother Myron...!'
Myron Zipl.
As he recalled the cries of his brothers during their lives, something swelled up in his chest.
Midor couldn't understand it all this time. Myron was killed by Runcandel, who was living triumphantly, but Zipl hadn't taken proper revenge.
Crackling, clattering...!
As Midor injected magic into the cube, the blue glow became even more intense. It was a bright light that could stand out even under the dark storm of the energy needles.
'What is that blue light?'
Jindo was far away, looking at the blue light of the cube.
'It doesn't seem like magic, maybe an artifact?'
It wasn't clearly visible due to the black needles. But at a glance, it was clearly a type of artifact he didn't know.
He also had a bad feeling. The sinister expression that suddenly seemed to burst into laughter at any moment in this crisis was also unpleasant.
The expression that those with a hidden move would show before revealing it.
Murakan was also narrowing his eyes at Midor's appearance.
[In any era, there are foolish people who insist on bringing death upon themselves.]
"Puhahaha, Kuhahahahaha!"
Midor suddenly leaned back and burst into laughter. The cube in his hand was floating in the air with each side open.
"Runcandel of the 12th generation, true Runcandel, and the black dragon Murakan! I've been waiting for this day. The day I can soothe my brother Myron's soul with your filthy blood...!"
[I can't allow that. I'll make you disappear.]
Kwaaaaa-!
Murakan fired his breath towards Midor and the mages of Zipl.
It was a breath filled with considerable emotion and anger. It meant a stronger force than the one that had obliterated the best warrior of the White Wolf tribe, leaving only his ankle behind.
Moreover, with the energy needles that were scattered along the path of his breath added, it became a scale that seemed to have slightly reduced a mountain range.
Only Murakan himself and Jin were the ones who could completely block that breath here.
The moment that breath struck Zipl's camp, Midor and the surviving mages had no choice but to panic with their eyes wide open.
"Ah, it's still open!"
"We need to block...!"
The desperate cries of the elders were cut short as they were swept away by the breath, turning into black particles.
The other wizards also exerted all their strength to create a protective barrier, but it was too much. Murakan's breath mercilessly ravaged the defense line of the Ziepl.
It was like a war chariot rolling down a steep hill, smashing dozens of houses before coming to a stop.
The breath that Murakan casually released turned about thirty elders into dust and shattered the protective barrier formed in front of Midor until it finally stopped.
The excited, laughing expression full of anticipation was now gone.
Midor merely blinked, feeling like his entire body was drained. His confidence in activating the hexahedron had already been greatly shaken.
'...Is this really the breath released without any warning or preparation?'
Midor felt a sharp intuition that he had miscalculated.
He had sensed it a little when the black thorns began to fall.
Whether this was really the right time to carry out his revenge.
It was already too late to recalculate. Moreover, Murakan was even more enraged by the sight of Midor surviving the breath. His pride was wounded.
["Blocked? Uh, blocked? You're insane, out of your mind, really? Hah, this little one... It's annoying."]
Murakan's speech was somewhat unusual due to his anger, but the enemies felt even more scared because of it. A capricious and misaligned strongman was always terrifying.
Huuup!
This time, Murakan took a deep breath. He properly gathered his strength to unleash his breath.
The soundless energy thorns ceased for a moment. The energy used for the thorn storm was added to the breath as a result.

The ground, where the energy thorns had stopped, looked desolate like a magical artillery testing ground. There was not a single flat surface left, and the corpses with only parts of their bodies remaining rolled like dust.

The remaining members of Biment's group barely managed to hold onto their souls and reorganize their ranks, while the beastmen of Kinzelro lost their minds completely, indiscriminately relieving themselves and crying out loud.
On Ziepl's side, only Midor and a few elders were left trembling.
In front of Jin, Sandra Ziepl was regenerating herself, slowly regaining her human form.
The sound of the gears turning was noticeably slower than before.
'Looking at this, it makes me think that it's really more amazing than the power of time.'

The power of time was indeed incredible, but as far as Jin knew, it was impossible to recover to this extent after suffering such fatal damage. Even Quicantel couldn't restore a body that had been dissected to the flesh.
'The power of the Magic Stone and the biological golem. It seems certain that both are being used together. If Ziepl can continuously create beings like Sandra...'
A memory from his past life suddenly came to mind.
The mirror, the spring of magical power.

In his previous life, Ziepl had obtained that mysterious power of Colon and continuously produced 7-star wizards without rest. Those mass-produced wizards, called assembly-line wizards, were then used to further solidify Ziepl's dominance.
Sandra's regenerative power was not comparable to the mass-produced wizards of the past life.
Is it due to my regression?
Could his own regression have stimulated Ziepl and had a significant impact on their research direction or achievements? Thus, is Runecandle now at a greater disadvantage than before?
Such a thought suddenly crossed his mind, but Jin soon shook his head.

"No, now that I think about it, Zifl couldn't have dominated that much with just mass-produced magicians. Even if there were a few of them with 7-star magic power, they couldn't handle proper 9 or 10-star magicians."
Back then, mass-produced magicians were probably just prototypes or materials for creating a 'weapon' like Sandra Zifl.

"At that time, mass-produced magicians were tools for promoting Zifl's dominance externally, while in reality, creatures like Sandra Zifl were being mass-produced and fighting battles that were not exposed to the media."
In Jin's current life, they didn't obtain the Mirror, so the likelihood of their research on biological golems being much slower than in their past life was high.
Even with that assumption, Zifl's biological golem had already reached this level. Coming back again and again even after being disassembled dozens of times.
"Moreover, I don't think the secret of Zifl I'll see today is everything..."
The glowing hexahedron.
A strong curiosity arose as to what it could be, as Midor confidently showed off.
Although the momentum seemed to have been broken by one breath.
"This...luck...son of a b*tch...stop..."
Sandra, whose face had partially returned, was the first to speak.
Midor was listening carefully. In the near silence created when the energy needles stopped, they could hear each other's breath.
However, Midor pretended not to hear Sandra's command and overcame his fear.
And he thought this.
"Yes, we can win. Don't be afraid. Today is the day when we can surely drink the blood of our enemies from a pure gold cup."
There is no reason not to do so with my brother.
Midor knelt down and respectfully raised his hands as if calling to a deity.
It was Midor's own ritual, completely unrelated to the 'complete opening' of the hexahedron. A ritual to welcome and show respect to his long-lost brother.
Hwooosh!
Light flowed like water from the fully opened faces. The light pouring from the hexahedron surged like waves in the air.
The dark, gloomy blue light beams seemed to be painting a picture on the canvas of space.
Except for Zifl, it was a strange sight that none of those who had lived for three thousand years, including Murakan, had ever seen before.
'The lights are forming something...ah, this is crazy.'
Jin, who had been watching the progress of the hexahedron's light for a moment, had to suppress the absurd curses that came to his mind.
The first thing the light formed was a human being.
It was Myron Zifl.
"Brother, welcome...!"
Midor raised his head and looked up at Myron with sparkling eyes.
Before they knew it, Myron had become a form made of not light, but a material with texture and weight.
However, unlike when they met in Colon, he didn't look like a completely living person.
His skin was dark blue like an old corpse, and parts of it were peeled away, revealing bones, teeth, and internal organs. His pupils were dark and dull, making him look like a moving corpse.
Moreover, Myron wasn't the only thing formed by the light of the hexahedron.
A ship.
Zyphl's decisive weapon, a symbol of the sky's disaster, a flying ship with a similar shape to Cozak.
The dark blue ship was even larger than Cozak, exuding an even greater sense of power based on its appearance alone.
Inside the ship were countless magicians, all formed from light, ready for boarding.
In other words, a Zyphl ship and army had suddenly been formed in the middle of the island.
The shocking sight made everyone forget what they were going to say, holding onto their sanity.
Even Jin's eyes widened, speechless.
[The air is nice here, Midor.]
Finally, Myron spoke with a gentle yet dignified voice, and Midor's face seemed to be on the verge of tears with emotion.
Now, with his brother, they could take revenge on their enemies and gain their father's recognition...!
His entire body trembled with excitement from the certainty that began with that belief. For a moment, doubting the power of his brother, his ship, and his army seemed foolish.
[And it's been a while, Jin Lun Khan...]
[Ah, I was watching what the heck was going on, and then something like this popped up. Huh? Unlucky!]
That's when it happened.
Murakan released the breath he had been holding.
Kwaaaaaaah-!
An energy far denser than the black spikes that had been pouring down was rushing toward Myron and his army.
Neither Midor nor Myron.
Neither of them thought that the breath could destroy the ship.
That's why they only planned to continue their intimidating dialogue and attacks after defending themselves once.
However, in the next moment, the giant ship formed by the light was so easily...
As if a burnt rice paper was burning in a torch, it was simply and completely destroyed by Murakan's breath, with the center being penetrated.
Kudududuk, kaduduk, kigigigigik!
Boom, bang! Gggggguk! Ping! Taetang!
Myron and Midor couldn't help but doubt their ears at the sound of the ship breaking. The sound seemed strange and unreal to the siblings.
[These worthless guys are just making things heavier, really. They're going to die.]
Murakan just snorted in derision.
